query:
In the discussion of mono pressings versus fold-down stereo cuts, one member argues that listening will show you the difference even where measurements look clean. Who actually made that argument?

Options:
A. Bram
B. Marcy
C. Theo
D. Felix
context:
[1] (about=Theo, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:14:00) Bram is right. I would add: even where measurements are clean, the sound character of a mono cut still differs in ways the measurements undersell. in my view this is one place where listening leads.
[2] (about=Bram, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:11:00) good question Dev, both. mono uses a horizontal-only cutting head and a dedicated mono tape if one exists, fold-down is a stereo cut summed to mono playback. they sound different. the mono cut is louder and more present, the fold-down is just half a stereo. listening tests will show you, even without measurements.
[3] (about=Bram, core, t2 @2026-01-19T18:51:00) mono uses horizontal-only cutting head and dedicated mono tape; fold-down is stereo cut summed to mono; mono is louder and more present.
[4] (about=Dev, core, t2 @2026-01-19T18:51:00) asked about difference between mono pressing and fold-down stereo; confused by conflicting info.
[5] (about=Dev, said_by=Marcy, profile, t8 @2026-02-09T19:17:00) Marcy says both, mostly mastering; Mobile Fidelity late 70s to early 80s hold up because cut hot with headroom.
[6] (about=Ines, core, t8 @2026-02-09T19:17:00) Ines agrees with Maeve; saw a Heart cassette with louder cut than LP; someone is doing god's work.
[7] (about=Lina, episodic, t8 @2026-02-09T19:27:00) Dev, I have changed on this. I had a hearing test last week. The audiologist suggested some mid-range compensation. I have started doing focused, louder sessions in the evening. Beethoven 9 last night at concert level, alone with the Quad ESLs. It was different.
[8] (about=Maeve, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:30:00) okay personal news, my grandmother passed last month and I inherited her console stereo!!! a 1962 Magnavox astro-sonic, it is gigantic and gorgeous. I have moved my primary listening from the studio nearfields to the console. it is a different relationship to listening, the speakers are integral, the cabinet is the room, and grandma is in the wood. I'm not going back.
[9] (about=Marcy, core, t2 @2026-01-19T18:51:00) DG bass character was tape-stage decision more than pressing; 2018 thinning is transfer choice not mastering; Esoteric does cleanest digital.
[10] (about=Olin, core, t16 @2026-03-09T17:40:00) revising position: hi-res streams from a serious orchestra archive can equal or beat reissued analog; Berlin Phil Digital Concert Hall subscription changed his view
[11] (about=Quint, episodic, t12 @2026-02-23T19:02:00) okay something I never thought Id say out loud. my daughter set up tidal on the shop laptop christmas time. I was going to ignore it and my hands have been busy on a cabinet. and now I find myself listening to it 4 hours at a stretch in the workshop. its convenient. at home I still play vinyl exclusively but at the shop tidal is what I'm doing. youngsters were right about convenience, the music is the same.
[12] (about=Sander, core, t2 @2026-01-19T18:51:00) found Blue Note original mono pressings at estate sale, family wanted them gone.
[13] (about=Theo, core, t2 @2026-01-19T18:51:00) sound character of mono cut differs in ways measurements undersell; listening leads in this case.
[14] (about=Yuko, core, t4 @2026-01-26T18:38:00) Yuko says conversational volume is the right level for cello recordings; dynamic range is preserved, most people lose it by playing too loud.
[15] (about=Yuko, core, t2 @2026-01-19T18:51:00) measurements undersell because typical set was designed for stereo; new protocols catch what Theo describes; conclusion is measurement vocabulary needs updating, not that listening leads.
